title: pairwise-rendezvous-eager-fusion-kv-serialize
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: In multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads we observed recurring p99 spikes driven by (1) small allreduce latency on dozens of layer-level tensors and (2) KV cache serialization/deserialization overhead when checkpointing/sharing KV shards across ranks. This PR implements a pairwise rendezvous allreduce path with eager micro-fusion for small tensors, plus a lightweight on-wire KV serialization elimination for hot-path checkpoints to reduce CPU->GPU stall. Approach: 1) Introduce pairwise asynchronous rendezvous that groups tensor allreduces into stable peer pairs when topology and bandwidth permit, reducing NCCL launch overhead in small-message regimes. 2) Add an eager micro-fusion pass that merges consecutive small kernels (<= 64KB) into a single fused kernel when safe to do so. 3) Replace the baseline KV cache checkpoint format with an in-place delta shipping mode: small KV windows are exchanged via a direct GPU-to-GPU buffer without an intermediate host-serialized blob. 4) Integrate the new paths into continuous batching so that prefix KV warmup keeps the fused path primed and avoids first-request stalls. Compatibility: The pairwise rendezvous falls back to the legacy allreduce when topology changes, PCIe-only nodes, or when NCCL reports stream conflicts. The KV delta shipping is opt-in by config (kvcache.delta_mode=true) and guarded by runtime checks for pinned memory and CUDA IPC availability. Commits: "initial pairwise rendezvous implementation", "add eager micro-fusion kernelizers and tests", "kv delta shipping wire format and runtime guards", "continuous-batching integration and priming", "benchmark results and tuning knobs". Changed areas: runtime/tp/collectives.cc, runtime/tp/pairwise_rendezvous.h, runtime/kvcache/delta_ship.cc, runtime/kernels/fusion_pass.cc, runtime/serving/continuous_batcher.cc, tests/tp/collective_integration_test.cc, bench/benchmarks/tp_smallmsg_allreduce.py. Performance: On 8xA100-80GB pods with NVLink, synthetic TP passbench shows p50 token latency -3%, p95 -7%, p99 -10% for small message micro-batched workloads; end-to-end throughput for 4-token streaming scenarios improved +12% at equal SLO. KV checkpoint hot-path CPU time dropped ~65% for small window checkpoints (<=1MB) and median request CPU tail reduced by ~18%. Safety and testing: Added unit tests for rendezvous fallback, fusion correctness tests with random shapes, and integration tests exercising kvcache.delta_mode across mixed topologies. Bench harness: repeated runs across three nodes with network emulation to verify regressions. Rollback plan: feature gated by runtime flags and config; immediate rollback possible via flipping kvcache.delta_mode=false and disabling pairwise_rendezvous in cluster config. Impact and risk: Low risk when flags off. With flags on, risk surface includes corner NCCL stream ordering issues, which are mitigated by conservative stream-affinity checks and an emergency fallback that forces legacy path on NCCL errors. Related work: ENG-2314 (small-message collective perf), ENG-2389 (kvcache repartitioning).

performance_benchmarks: Hardware: 8xA100-80GB NVLink, 3xDGX nodes. Workloads: micro-batched small message TP (avg tensor 16KB), continuous-batching streaming 4-token profile. Results: p99 latency reduced 10% (baseline 42ms -> 38ms), throughput +12% under load, KV checkpoint CPU time -65% for <=1MB shards. Repeatability: 5 runs, stdev <2% for throughput.
release_notes: Introduce opt-in pairwise rendezvous path that reduces small-message allreduce latency and an opt-in KV delta shipping mode to reduce KV cache serialization CPU time. Feature is off by default and gated behind kvcache.delta_mode and pairwise_rendezvous flags. Recommended for TP workloads with many small tensors.
